        ### Question
        A 3-year-old child referred for genetic consultation to assess psychomotor retardation, language delay and hyperactivity without significant dysmorphic features or associated malformations. He is the first child of a healthy, young and non-consanguineous couple. A maternal uncle has mental retardation and the maternal grandmother presented early ovarian failure. Which of the following diagnostic tests would be the most appropriate to establish the diagnosis?

        ### Options
        opa. Genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene.
opb. Complete metabolic study.
opc. High resolution karyotype
opd. Psychometric evaluation

CHAIN: "Child has no significant dysmorphic features" -> "Less likely to be a chromosomal abnormality" -> "High resolution karyotype may not be necessary" -> "Family history suggests genetic disorder" -> "FMR1 gene testing is indicated" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Psychometric evaluation assesses cognitive function" -> "Does not establish a genetic diagnosis" -> "Genetic testing needed for definitive diagnosis" -> "FMR1 gene triplet expansion testing is most appropriate" -> 75%
